text:
Logan Stanley made the news this weekend for the wrong reason: the NHL fined him the maximum for slashing Nico Hischier in Saturday's loss to the Devils. It was the kind of play that follows a big, physical defenseman around, and it landed in a week when the Islanders need him more than ever.

With Ryan Pulock out, Stanley's minutes have jumped about two and a half a night over his last ten games, to over 22, and he and Adam Pelech have carried the penalty kill on some nights, as Stefen Rosner noted. The five-on-five numbers are better than you might expect: the Islanders take about 54% of the expected goals with him on the ice, six points better than without him, though some of that comes with good fortune on goals.

He's not an offensive player: no goals and five assists in 16 games, and only seven shots despite a slap shot NHL Edge rates among the hardest in the league. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season in Winnipeg. Our range has him at 24 to 43 points over a full season, which is generous. His job is minutes and the penalty kill, and staying out of the box.
headline: Stanley's bigger role, and a fine
